findings.title: Successful charge can leave key permanently stuck in completed state if receipt storage fails
findings.evidence: After the gateway returns, the code writes the receipt to the store without any cleanup path if that write raises, so the key remains in '_in_flight' forever and all retries raise DuplicateRequestInFlight instead of returning the original receipt.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the completion step so failures do not leave the key poisoned. For example, ensure the in-flight marker is cleared on any exception from completion, or make completion atomic and non-throwing for the supported store implementation. Add a test where store.complete raises after a successful gateway charge and verify a retry can proceed or recover deterministically.

findings.title: Catching BaseException abandons the key on KeyboardInterrupt/SystemExit, undermining the documented crash-retry behavior
findings.evidence: The exception handler clears the in-flight key for every BaseException, including process-termination exceptions, even though the docstring says retries after a crash should rely on the provider-side idempotency key.
findings.recommendation: Catch Exception instead of BaseException so termination signals are not treated like ordinary request failures. If you need special handling for cancellation, handle those cases explicitly and document the semantics.
